title: Discover and review Power Pages sites with Power Platform inventory (public preview)
summary: Support for Power Pages sites in Power Platform inventory is now in public preview. Administrators can now discover and review sites across environments in one place, alongside apps, flows, and agents.
body_markdown:
Support for Power Pages sites in Power Platform inventory is now in public preview. Administrators can now discover and review sites across environments in one place, alongside apps, flows, and agents. This central view makes it easier to find sites, coordinate with site owners, and support day-to-day site administration, while including Power Pages in broader operational and governance reviews across Power Platform.


# What’s new


- **Discover sites across environments.** Find Power Pages sites from **Manage > Inventory** in the Power Platform admin center. Search, filter, and sort the inventory to focus on the sites you need.
- **Review sites alongside other resources.** Include Power Pages in the same inventory experience as apps, flows, and agents for a broader view of Power Platform adoption across your organization.
- **Query inventory for reporting and workflows.** Query Power Pages site data through Azure Resource Graph, the Power Platform API, or the Power Platform for Admins V2 connector to build reports, support recurring operational and governance reviews, and use the results in your workflows.
- **Export for further analysis.** Download the inventory to a CSV file for reporting and reviews.


# Why this matters


With sites in inventory, administrators have one place to start for both day-to-day requests and scheduled reviews:


- **Support everyday site administration.** Locate a portal, identify its owner, then use the inventory as a starting point for changes or support coordination.
- **Focus configuration reviews.** Prioritize which sites need a closer look, e.g., identify sites that allow anonymous access or developer sites with public visibility, then work with their owners to confirm these settings match the intended audience.
- **Support ownership transitions.** Keep sites running when people move on from your organization, e.g., find sites owned by departing employees so you can coordinate handoffs and maintain business continuity.
- **Bring sites into broader planning and governance.** See where sites are distributed across environments and include them in operational planning and governance reviews alongside other Power Platform resources.


For example, when a support request comes in for a customer or partner portal, an administrator can find the site and its owner to coordinate the investigation or during a scheduled review, the same team can check which sites allow anonymous access, confirming it’s intentional for a public site and taking a closer look at a partner portal meant for signed-in users.


Inventory helps administrators decide where to focus their attention. It doesn’t change site settings or replace a detailed site security review.


# How to get started


To view Power Pages sites in inventory, you must have the **Global Administrator** , **Power Platform Administrator** , or **Dynamics 365 Administrator** role.


1. Sign in to the[Power Platform admin center](https://aka.ms/ppac) .
2. Go to **Manage > Inventory** .
3. Filter the **Item type** column to **Sites** .
4. Search, filter, and sort the results to find the sites you want to review, such as sites in a specific environment or sites owned by a particular user.
5. Use **Add or remove columns** next to the search box to choose the columns displayed in your view.


# Learn more


See[Power Pages Inventory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-pages/admin/power-pages-inventory) and[Power Platform inventory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/power-platform-inventory) to learn about the inventory experience and access options.
To query inventory data for your reports and workflows, see[programmatic access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/power-platform-inventory#programmatic-access) for setup and authentication requirements. We’d love to hear your feedback! Share your thoughts in the[Power Pages community forum](https://ideas.powerpages.microsoft.com/d365community/forum/1edba0ec-30cf-ec11-a7b5-000d3a545c96)
